title: Hand Hygiene
description: Proper hand hygiene is one of the most important methods for preventing healthcare-associated infections.
keywords: hand washing hand hygiene infection control غسل اليدين مكافحة العدوى
overview: Hand hygiene is the process of cleaning hands to remove microorganisms and reduce the transmission of infection.
indications: Before performing a clean or aseptic procedure.
steps: Remove rings, watches and bracelets when appropriate.
Wet hands with clean running water.
Apply an adequate amount of soap.
Rub all surfaces of the hands thoroughly.
Clean between fingers and around the thumbs.
Rinse hands thoroughly.
Dry hands with a clean disposable towel.
Use the towel to turn off the faucet when necessary.
precautions: Keep fingernails short and clean.
Avoid artificial nails in clinical areas when prohibited.
Cover cuts or abrasions with appropriate dressings.
notes: Hand hygiene should be performed according to the clinical situation and institutional infection-control policy.

title: Vital Signs Assessment
description: Basic assessment of temperature, pulse, respiration and blood pressure.
keywords: vital signs temperature pulse respiration blood pressure العلامات الحيوية
overview: Vital signs provide important information about a patient's physiological status.
steps: Explain the procedure to the patient.
Perform hand hygiene.
Ensure the patient is in an appropriate position.
Measure temperature using the appropriate method.
Assess pulse rate and rhythm.
Count respiratory rate and observe respiratory pattern.
Measure blood pressure using the correct cuff size.
Document the findings.
precautions: Use the correct equipment.
Use an appropriate blood pressure cuff size.
Compare abnormal findings with previous readings when available.
notes: Abnormal vital signs should be assessed in relation to the patient's overall clinical condition.

title: Patient Bed Bath
description: Basic principles of providing a bed bath while maintaining patient comfort, privacy and safety.
keywords: bed bath bathing patient care حمام المريض العناية بالمريض
overview: A bed bath is provided to patients who are unable to bathe independently.
indications: Patients who cannot safely use the bathroom.
steps: Explain the procedure to the patient.
Provide privacy and maintain a comfortable room temperature.
Perform hand hygiene and prepare equipment.
Maintain the patient's privacy throughout the procedure.
Clean the body systematically.
Change water or supplies when necessary.
Dry the skin carefully, especially skin folds.
Reposition the patient safely.
Document the care provided when required.
precautions: Maintain patient dignity and privacy.
Avoid exposing unnecessary areas of the body.
Check water temperature before use.
Observe the skin for redness, irritation or pressure areas.
notes: Patient comfort, dignity and safety should be maintained throughout the procedure.

title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
description: Selection and appropriate use of personal protective equipment in healthcare settings.
keywords: PPE gloves gown mask goggles personal protective equipment معدات الوقاية الشخصية
overview: Personal protective equipment is used to reduce exposure to infectious materials and protect healthcare workers and patients.
indications: Potential contact with blood or body fluids.
Droplet or airborne precautions according to the clinical situation.
steps: Assess the expected exposure risk.
Select appropriate PPE.
Perform hand hygiene.
Don PPE in the appropriate sequence.
Perform the required patient-care activity.
Remove PPE carefully to avoid contamination.
Perform hand hygiene after removal.
precautions: Use PPE appropriate to the expected exposure.
Avoid touching the face while wearing contaminated gloves.
Dispose of single-use PPE according to facility policy.
notes: PPE selection should follow the healthcare facility's infection-prevention policies and the type of anticipated exposure.

title: Medication Administration Safety
description: Essential safety principles for medication administration by nurses.
keywords: medication administration medication safety drugs الأدوية إعطاء الدواء
overview: Medication administration requires careful verification, accurate documentation and monitoring for therapeutic effects and adverse reactions.
steps: Verify the medication order.
Confirm the patient's identity using approved identifiers.
Check the medication, dose, route and timing.
Assess relevant patient information before administration.
Administer the medication using the appropriate technique.
Monitor the patient as appropriate.
Document medication administration.
precautions: Check allergies before administration.
Follow institutional medication-safety policies.
Clarify unclear or incomplete medication orders.
Never administer a medication that cannot be safely identified.
notes: Medication administration should always follow the current prescription and the policies of the healthcare facility.

title: Pressure Injury Prevention
description: Basic nursing measures to reduce the risk of pressure injuries in vulnerable patients.
keywords: pressure injury pressure ulcer prevention skin care قرح الفراش الوقاية
overview: Pressure injury prevention focuses on reducing prolonged pressure and protecting skin and tissue integrity.
indications: Patients at increased risk of skin breakdown.
steps: Assess the patient's skin and risk factors.
Keep the skin clean and dry.
Reposition the patient according to the care plan.
Use appropriate pressure-relieving surfaces when indicated.
Encourage adequate nutrition and hydration when appropriate.
Document skin assessment and preventive interventions.
precautions: Avoid unnecessary friction and shear.
Inspect pressure-prone areas regularly.
Do not massage areas of suspected tissue injury.
notes: Prevention should be individualized according to the patient's mobility, skin condition and overall clinical status.
